entries.title: Earning coins
q: how do i get village coins
how can i earn gold coins
entries.answer: Every coin comes from somebody in the towns. The quickest: sell what you carry at the town store, or take a shift from the jobs board (press U).
more: Sell goods at a town's counters, deliver its Wanted orders, take paid shifts or a job, do quests and errands, run a shop or stall, earn night bounties, carry haul contracts, or own houses and land that pay rent.
steps: Quick start: sell what you carry at the town store (Sell tab) or deliver a Wanted order.
Steady: a standing job pays every morning for each day worked.
Bigger: open a shop (U → Open a shop) or start a business.
Check U → The Earnings page for the ways to earn here now.
tips: Every payment is told at once in chat and as a toast, and booked in your finances.
Gold turns into coin at a stall's counter or the bank's money changer: eight or nine coins a bar.

entries.title: The Village Coin
entries.answer: The Village Coin is the towns' money. It can't be crafted: earn it, or trade gold for it at a stall's counter or the bank.
more: It has no recipe: a town strikes it at its mint (from the Iron Age, nine coins to a gold bar it buys), and you can turn gold into coin at a market stall's counter (eight coins an ingot) or the bank's money changer.
steps: Bring gold ingots to a stall's counter or the bank's counter (money changer).
tips: A coin is always worth a coin, whatever minting it took.

entries.title: Selling goods to the town
q: how do i sell items to the village
entries.answer: Each counter buys its own trade's goods. Right-click the town store's counter and open its Sell tab.
more: Each counter buys its own trade's goods: the store what the market deals in (and sticks, cobblestone, string, coal, planks), the café the kitchen's, the tavern the cellar's, the smith metal and fuel, the tailor wool, string, leather and dye.
steps: Deliver Wanted orders at the top first (a premium).
Sell 1 lot, a stack or all.
tips: The price falls as the counter's stock fills, then stops: sell a glut and you get less and less.
The store also buys finds: museum pieces, written books and explorer maps, a few a day.
warn: Buying a lot and selling it back loses money.

entries.title: Wanted orders
q: what does the town need me to bring
entries.answer: Wanted orders are what the town is short of, paid at a premium for three days. Deliver them on the store counter's Sell tab.
more: Hold the goods and Deliver on the store's Sell tab, or at the town board or storehouse: paid at once.

entries.title: Buying from the town
q: how do i buy food from the village
can i buy from the stores
entries.answer: Buy at the town's counters (shop, store, café, tavern), or ask a folk 'For sale?' (Trade, then Shop).
more: Friends and citizens can also ask the stores for things ('Could I have 8 bread?').
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Shop → For sale? · Ask the stores…

entries.title: Asking the stores
q: can i take from the village storage
borrow a pickaxe from the village
entries.answer: Ask the storekeeper for something from the stores: 'could I have 16 bread?'. Friends and citizens get a stack a day free.
more: A friend or citizen gets food and goods free, up to a stack a day, and tools, weapons and armour lent; a stranger pays the market price and a little over.
controls: [Right-click] the storekeeper → Trade → Shop → Ask the stores…
warn: Return what's lent (Hand over) within five days, or it's remembered against you.
Taking from the stores' chests yourself is theft unless you're a citizen.

entries.title: Haggling
q: how do i get a discount
entries.answer: Ask the storekeeper, shopkeeper or cook 'Haggle' (Trade, then Shop) for 5 to 20 in the hundred off for the day.
more: A generous one, or a friend, is easily talked round; a shrewd elder's town is not.
The discount (5 to 20 in the hundred) holds at the stores and counters for the day.
controls: [Right-click] storekeeper / shopkeeper / cook → Trade → Shop → Haggle
tips: Other discounts stack as lines in the basket: friend, citizen (a tenth at the shop and café), the town's medal or key.

entries.title: Made to order, mending and the crafts' services
q: can a villager make me an item
can the smith repair my armour
entries.answer: Smiths, tailors and other crafts make things to order and mend what you carry. Ask them under Trade, then Shop: 'Make me…' or 'Mend this'.
more: Ask a smith, tailor, smelter or enchanter 'Make me…' (Trade → Shop): it's made from its recipe out of what you carry and the town can spare, ready the next day.
The crafts have their own: a tailor 'Make me something', a brewer 'A potion', an enchanter 'Enchant this', a beekeeper 'Honey'.
steps: For mending: hold the worn tool, weapon or armour and ask the smith 'Mend this' (or use the smithy's anvil screen).
For an order: Trade → Shop → Make me… and finish the sentence ('Make me an iron sword').
Come back the next day and ask for it.
controls: [Right-click] smith → Trade → Shop → Mend this · Make me…
Tailor / brewer / enchanter / beekeeper → Trade → Shop
tips: Mending costs the metal at market price plus a two-coin fee; bring your own metal and pay only the fee.
Outdoor trades sell their goods too: produce, timber, fresh fish, wool, a horse, coal and ore, arrows.

entries.title: Bulk orders and supply contracts
q: sign a contract with the village
entries.answer: Order goods by the stack ('I'd like to order 256 cobblestone'), or sign a supply contract to bring the town what it's short of each week.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Shop → Order goods…
warn: Miss two weeks of a contract and it lapses, and the town thinks less of you.

entries.title: The auction
entries.answer: On market day a town of twelve or more holds an auction on the square. Right-click the auctioneer to bid, or to put up what you hold.
more: On market day a town of twelve or more (Stone Age on) holds an auction on the square: its rare finds, the museum's spares, a merchant's curio, and anything players put up.
Right-click the auctioneer: bid the next step (or two), type a bid of your own, and put the thing in your hand up for auction.
tips: Lots start at a reserve of half their worth.
The market toll (a tax) may take a share of what you sell there.

entries.title: Prices and where things are dear
q: buy low sell high between towns
entries.answer: Each town has a going price for everything, dear when it's short and cheap in a glut. Ask any folk 'Prices' (Trade, then Money).
more: Ask any folk 'Prices' (Trade → Money) or 'Where's iron dear?' for here and the towns round about; the town's books' Prices page and Dashboard show the index.
tips: Buy cheap in one town and sell dear in another: the Earnings page lists the best prices for what you carry.

entries.title: The market (the storehouse's bid and ask)
q: who pays for things in town
entries.answer: The storehouse is the town's market: it buys what producers bring in and sells to everyone else. The town's books' Market page shows it.
more: A new town's first days are a free commons; on Market Opening Day the stock becomes the market's and each founder who works the land gets its own business.
controls: Town's books → Economy → Market · Dashboard · Money

entries.title: The town's treasury
q: how does the town get money
entries.answer: The treasury is the town's purse: it pays wages and builds. Give to it from U, then Everything you can do, then the Money tab.
more: Its money comes from what the town made each day (sold to passing traders), taxes, fees, rents and the market's surplus.
The town's books' Money page shows its accounts.
controls: [U] → Everything you can do → Money → Give it to the treasury

entries.title: Trade between towns
q: do towns trade with each other
entries.answer: Towns trade what one can spare and another lacks, by caravan and envoy. The town's books' Trade page shows it.
more: Towns trade what one can spare and another is short of: by caravans on the roads, envoys' deals, and on the region's market.
Ask a folk to broker a trade pact with a neighbour ('we should make a pact with Kingsgate').
The Trade and Region pages show it.

entries.title: Caravans and a trade route of your own
entries.answer: Caravans carry goods between towns every two days. Fifty coins charters a trade route of your own that pays you a tenth of every load.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Services → Charter a route · Guard a caravan

entries.title: The emerald trader and vanilla villagers
entries.answer: A town's emerald trader trades with vanilla villagers for what the town can't make. Ask it 'What the villagers sell'.
more: From the Stone Age a town of twelve or more takes on an emerald trader: it walks to the game's villager villages, sells the town's surplus for emeralds, and buys what the town can't make (enchanted books, a bell, maps).
Ask it 'What the villagers sell', or 'Find us something' ('Find us a Mending book').
controls: [Right-click] the emerald trader → Trade → Shop → What the villagers sell · Find us something

entries.title: Forged Coin
entries.answer: A forged coin is a forger's fake, worth only its copper. Three of them make a copper ingot back.
more: Nothing forged is ever sold at the shop or auction.
